idiom_name: pugixml DOM building + save_to_stream (or libxslt XSLT)
implementation_notes: The modern C++ default builds the markup as a pugixml tree: xml_document is the root, append_child creates elements, node_pcdata nodes hold text (escaped on save) and save/save_to_stream serializes, so a mutable DOM plus one serializer replaces the hand-written Transformer. libxslt drives a stylesheet when the source is already XML (xsltParseStylesheetFile/xsltApplyStylesheet), and a per-type transformer class remains the right shape when the output is conditional HTML rather than a data tree.
pitfalls: Text must live in PCDATA nodes: append_child(node_pcdata).set_value(...) is required; setting a value on an element node silently produces empty output.
xml_node and xml_attribute are non-owning handles: they dangle once the document or parent node is destroyed, so the xml_document must outlive every handle.
The XSLT route inherits the C API's ownership rules: free the stylesheet and documents explicitly or leak on every request.

variants.name: libxslt stylesheet over serialized XML
variants.implementation_notes: Stylesheet over an XML serialization: compile with xsltParseStylesheetFile and apply with xsltApplyStylesheet exactly as in C (or use Xalan-C++ where an XSLT 2.0-era processor is required). Choose it when the domain is already XML and presentation must change without a rebuild; keep the stylesheet compile step out of the request path.
pitfalls: Do not compile stylesheets per request: xsltParseStylesheetFile is expensive and the compiled object is meant to be reused.
libxslt processes untrusted stylesheets unsafely (filesystem and network access); only trusted stylesheets belong in a deployment.
